descriptionChirho: The physical organ of sight, used both literally (seeing, looking, blindness) and metaphorically (the eye as lamp of the body, evil eye, eyes of the heart for spiritual perception). Spanish 'ojos/ojo/de-ojos/de-ojo' are inflectional variants with prepositions. Hindi 'आँखें/आँखों/आँख' are plural, oblique plural, and singular of the same noun. Arabic 'عَينِ/عَينَين/عُيوناً/عَيْنًا' represent dual, broken plural, and accusative singular case forms of the root ʿ-y-n. Korean '눈/눈들을/눈들-의/눈-의/눈-을' differ only in plural marker and case particles. Swahili 'macho/jicho' are regular plural (ma-) and singular (ji-) of the same noun class 5/6. All three clusters are grammatical case and number variants of one sense across all 100 occurrences.
